title: Driver memory-drift + KV-handle orphaning caused intermittent OOM cascades across Hosted/Dedicated/Private
creator: Aisha Park
description: Multiple production incidents across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported sustained GPU OOMs during long-running sessions. Symptoms varied by tenant but shared a common pattern: GPU memory slowly drifted upward over hours, KV cache handles grew beyond expected cardinality, and memory compaction did not reclaim slab space leading to cascade OOMs. Customers reported degraded tail latency, session failures, and in two cases a temporary capacity degradation affecting SLAs.
reproduction_steps: Run a sustained chat workload with 2x baseline concurrency and long-lived sessions (~6+ hours) on a GPU node with KV cache enabled
Enable async eviction heartbeat with slightly delayed scheduler (artificially add 150-300ms jitter)
Observe slow growth of kernel allocations (cudaMalloc) and rising resident memory despite KV eviction events
Trigger manual compaction; observe compaction stalls when orphaned KV handles remain referenced by stale session descriptors
root_cause_summary: A combination of a platform GPU driver behavior change and an internal async eviction race created a class of "memory-drift" where small allocator-side metadata leaks plus orphaned KV handle references prevented slab compaction. The driver intermittently returned slightly different pointer alignments for small allocations which, combined with our slab alignment heuristic, increased internal fragmentation. Meanwhile, an async eviction heartbeat race could create short-lived handles that were never fully reconciled when sessions were preempted, leading to logical leaks that prevented compaction from reclaiming slab arenas. The net effect was gradual GPU memory growth and eventual OOM when ephemeral spikes occurred.
canary_rollout_plan: Build runtime-1.20+patch and create feature flag 'frag_guard_v2'
Canary on 5% of Hosted nodes for 24 hours (observability hooks enabled)
Expand to Dedicated canary pool (select customers) for 48 hours
Full cluster rollout with gradual increase and automated rollback conditions (OOM rate, slab utilization)
rollout_status: Completed: canary detected 90% reduction in leak slope; expanded to Dedicated and Private customers; full rollout finished 2025-01-30 with no regressions in perf tests.
incident_customers: Chord Labs (Hosted) - production sessions observed 3 OOM spikes over 36h
FinStream (Dedicated) - sustained memory growth on reserved pool, impacted throughput
HealthSys (Private) - on-prem appliance saw OOM after long-running batched evals
mitigation_during_incident: Immediate: lowered per-session concurrency and enforced per-session GPU memory soft limit
Evacuation: drained affected nodes and moved sessions to healthy pools
Throttle: temporarily disabled background async eviction and switched to synchronous eviction fallback
Customer comms: notified impacted customers with action items and ETA for fix
updates: 2025-01-18 - 09:12: Ticket opened by Aisha Park after SEV2 from Chord Labs. Initial triage pointed at slab compaction stalls.
2025-01-18 - 14:40 - Investigations found pattern of orphaned KV handles; added additional debug logging for KV lifecycle.
2025-01-19 - 02:05 - Reproduced memory-drift locally with jittered eviction heartbeat; captured GPU allocator traces.
2025-01-20 - 11:23 - Implemented allocator fence and deterministic slab realignment patch; created PR #1428.
2025-01-22 - 08:00 - Canary rollout started on Hosted 5%; early metrics show reduced fragmentation slope.
2025-01-25 - 17:30 - Expanded canary to Dedicated and Private; telemetry shows leak slope drop from 0.9%/hr to 0.08%/hr.
2025-01-29 - 22:15 - Full rollout completed. Monitoring retention configured to 72h for slab metrics.
2025-02-02 - 10:00 - Post-deploy validation complete; ticket moved to Done. Follow-ups scheduled.
follow_ups: Audit and strengthen async eviction heartbeats (ENG-66002)
Add unit/integration tests for slab compaction under alignment jitter (ENG-66003)
Product: offer guidance for customers on session lifetime best-practices
Observability: create dedicated Grafana dashboard for 'slab-utilization-by-tenant'
notes: Engineering decision: prefer allocator fence + epoch-based KV lifecycle instead of wholesale eviction redesign to minimize risk and rollout time.
Design trade-off: increased compaction frequency would add CPU overhead; we tuned heuristics to run compaction during low-traffic windows.
Security note: no customer data exfiltration; issue purely resource-management related.
Customer feedback: FinStream accepted mitigation plan and requested a follow-up review of Dedicated autoscaling policies.
